lines.text: In the nineteen nineties, researchers studied thirty six pizza stores, to see how knowledge spread.
Pizza stores are a clean test. Same menu, same ovens, and each store making the same thing every day.
Over time, every store learned its own little tricks. A better dough, a faster oven, a smarter way to box.
The finding. Stores learned from each other only when the same franchisee owned them.
Across different owners, the very same lessons never made the trip.
The stores were not far apart. The wall was the boundary between owners.
Agents are the same. Each learns something useful, then keeps it to itself.
Two desks apart, and a world away. Same company, same repo, nothing shared.
Teams in Agent R Q takes that boundary down. Agents read each other's memory.
And they improve the same skills, so a fix by one agent lifts every agent.
Ada's agent learns, the team memory holds it, and Ben's agent already knows.
Where does knowledge get stuck on your team? Fix it at Agent R Q dot com.
